summary: Encumbrance as numbers: DragonRealms' own burden rank read from Lich's ENC_MAP, plus a derived carried-item count that reaches inside containers and is reported as a floor. Also closes #562 (mock container fixtures could only draw the one state a live bridge can never produce).

coordination.notes: lich-scripts/companion_bridge.lic is the file PLAN_TO_1_0.md section 3 allows only one in-progress increment across lanes R/W/X/Y/Z. Checked before claiming: section 3.1's live-claims table has no R/W/X/Y/Z row, `git ls-remote --heads origin 'lane-w*'` returns nothing, and the only `[~]` increment in the plan is V2, which touches tools/break-check-tree.mjs. Extends rather than duplicates: `carriedItemCount` was published by W0 and is wired here for the first time; the container contents it sums are the ones W2 wired in the same file two commits ago, so nothing re-reads GameObj a second way. The burden ladder is READ from Lich (`Lich::DragonRealms::ENC_MAP`) rather than copied, for the reason the neighbouring balance/position fields already state - a second ladder in this repository would be free to drift from the one the game's own text is matched against. The two test-side ladders (protocol_harness.rb, encumbrance_test.rb) are deliberate labelled SUBSETS, not copies claiming fidelity; ruby/lich_stub.rb carries the full twelve entries because standing in for an absent Lich is that file's whole job. src/data/obstacles.ts's effectiveAthletics still substring-matches the word and collapses ranks 4-11 into one bucket - left alone on purpose: its multipliers have no published source, and rewriting them against the rank would have meant inventing numbers, which is the defect this increment exists to avoid. Recorded here rather than silently fixed.
